naslov: The Most Important Act of Worship – Prayer (Salah)

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

Nahmaduhu ta'ala wa nasta'inuhu wa nastaghfiruhu, wa na'udhu billahi min shururi anfusina wa min sayyi'ati a'malina. Man yahdihillahu fala mudilla lah, wa man yudlilhu fala hadiya lah. Ash-hadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, wa ash-hadu anna sayyidana wa nabiyyana Muhammadan 'abduhu wa habibuhu wa rasuluhu, arsalahullahu tabaraka wa ta'ala bil-huda wa dinil-haqqi li yuzhirahu 'alad-dini kullihi wa law karihal-kafirun. Fa salawatu Rabbi wa salamuhu 'alayhi wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi wa man sara 'ala nahjihi waqtafa atharahu ila yawmid-din. Ridwanullahi ta'ala 'alayna

wa 'alayhim ajma'in. Fa amma ba'd. Respected brothers, honoured believers! The most important act of worship that Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has prescribed for His servants is the prayer, salah.
Prayer is the pillar of the religion; prayer is the main symbol by which Muslims are recognised; prayer is the essence of obedience, devotion and gratitude to Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
Prayer is something without which faith can barely exist in a person, in an individual and in a community. Much can be said about the importance of prayer and the aspects of its significance.

Today I want to shed light on just one aspect of the importance of prayer, of how highly Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has raised this act of worship. And that is the fact that prayer was prescribed for every one of Allah's messengers.

So prayer was an obligation, a fard, for every one of Allah's messengers, from Adam, alayhis-salatu was-salam, to Muhammad, alayhis-salatu was-salam. That shows the importance of prayer, and in order to understand why prayer is so important, we must understand our need for prayer.

The Lord of all the worlds is ghaniyyun 'anil-'alamin, independent of all the worlds and of all creatures. He, jalla wa 'ala, is perfect and complete, but prayer is for our benefit. The Noble, Wise and Merciful Creator prescribed prayer for our own sake, because it is food for our soul and our hearts, and it is impossible for the soul and body to attain tranquillity, true balance and true humility without performing the prayer in its essence and being fully present in the prayer.

Allah the Exalted mentions in many places in the Qur'an that He commanded His messengers to perform the prayer. Speaking about Yunus, alayhis-salam (peace be upon him), He says… Yunus, alayhis-salam, who found himself in the belly of the whale, who was swallowed by the whale – a story mentioned in the Qur'an.

Allah says: had he not been among those who glorify Allah… Ibn Abbas says: had he not been among those who pray. Had he not performed the prayer, he would have remained there until the Day of Judgement. It was because of prayer that Allah, subhanahu, saved him then. Prayer is a shield; prayer protects a person.

Prayer connects you to the firmest support and the firmest strength and energy, and that is Allah the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala. When Ibrahim, alayhis-salatu was-salam, came to Mecca, it was a desert; there was nothing in Mecca.

He left his wife Hajar and Isma'il and turned away; when he climbed a small hill near Mecca – and Mecca was all hills – he began to supplicate to Allah, jalla wa 'ala: "Rabbana inni askantu min dhurriyyati bi wadin ghayri dhi zar'in 'inda baytikal-muharram."

Dear Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in this valley where nothing grows, by Your House, that is, next to the Ka'bah – for the Ka'bah existed even before Ibrahim, but its foundations had been lost.

"Dear Lord, so that they may establish the prayer." Look: the first thing Ibrahim, alayhis-salam, mentions is that his offspring should perform the prayer. And when He mentioned Isma'il, alayhis-salam,

Allah the Exalted, jalla sha'nuhu, says: Isma'il used to command his family to perform the prayer. Children and family should be taught to perform the prayer. And we should strive to perform the prayer in congregation at home.
Isma'il persisted in commanding prayer to his family and his children. And Ishaq – when Allah speaks about Ishaq, He says: "We commanded them to do good deeds and to establish the prayer."

Ishaq, alayhis-salam, the son of Ibrahim, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Imagine Musa, alayhis-salam, one of the five most chosen messengers. Musa is an incredible man. His story should be read over and over.

His story is complete. Only the story of the Messenger of Allah is more complete than his. For he was a husband, and a teacher, and a statesman, and a military commander, a leader. That is why his story… and a fighter in the way of Allah, jalla wa 'ala. That is why his story is mentioned so many times,

dozens of times in the Qur'an. Imagine the moment: Musa, alayhis-salam… How was he honoured? By speaking with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, by speaking with the Lord of all the worlds. If any one of us were given the opportunity to speak with some king, with an emperor, with the president of the most powerful country, we would prepare ourselves.
How will we dress, how will we [unclear], what will we wear? This is a conversation with the Lord of all the worlds. And do you know what Allah said to him first?
"Listen well, Musa: la ilaha illallah – there is no true deity except Me. Worship Me and establish the prayer,
establish the prayer in order to remember Me," Allah says to Musa, alayhis-salatu was-salam. When Dawud made a mistake and judged between two men without hearing both sides, he saw that he had erred.
And what did he do? What did he do? He said: "Astaghfirullah," he began… he rushed [unclear] to prayer. He hastened to go down in prostration to Allah, having first made ruku' (the bow).

And the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him): "Idha hazabahu amrun fazi'a ilas-salah." Whenever things became hard for the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in the most difficult moments he would stand up to pray. He would stand up to pray.

Obligatory or voluntary, two rak'ahs. That is where he sought comfort. That is where he drew energy and strength. Turn to Allah in prostration. Tell Him what you need. Ask of Him. For with Allah you are at your strongest.

And without His support and help we truly cannot do anything. Ask Allah for everything, and turn to Him in prostration for all your needs. When Sulayman, alayhis-salam… the rulers of today are nothing compared to Sulayman, alayhis-salam – what a ruler he was.

Allah subjected the whole earth to him, Allah subjected the wind to him, and people and jinn; everything was under the authority of Sulayman, alayhis-salam. And what did he use his authority for? Authority is used for the sake of truth and goodness, for guiding people and mankind towards goodness, for bringing or delivering benefit to people and protecting people from harm.

That was Sulayman, alayhis-salam. Politics and power should be in the service of truth and the preservation of religion. If they are not, then that is a disorder. And then chaos arises, as we are witnessing with all of this.

He loved horses. And one afternoon, after the Dhuhr prayer, he asked for all the horses to be brought out to him. You can imagine what horses they were – Arabian horses are especially famous in that region. And he was enjoying the display of his power, strength and so on.

And he forgot to pray the Asr prayer. He missed the Asr prayer unintentionally. And Allah, jalla wa 'ala… one prayer. Allah, jalla wa 'ala, then mentions in the Qur'an what he did with those horses: "Fa tafiqa mashan bis-suqi wal-a'naq."

"Rudduha 'alayya, fa tafiqa mashan bis-suqi wal-a'naq." Bring those horses back to me; all of them he [unclear], he slaughtered them all. Because whatever turns you away from the path of Allah, jalla wa 'ala, whatever turns you away from prayer, there is no khayr (good) in it. Do not allow anything, or any thing, or anyone, to turn you away from prayer.

Allah, jalla wa 'ala, says: "La tulhikum amwalukum wa la awladukum 'an dhikrillah." Do not let your children and your wealth divert you from the path of Allah. If the family diverts you from the path of Allah, then they are not a support; they are enemies. They are enemies.

Look [unclear]: yes, power; yes, authority; yes, wealth; yes, blessings; but all of it in the service of truth and goodness. And let prayer come first, and then arrange everything else. My dear brothers, we are witnesses to prayer having become a side activity for us. We run around, we work, we fire off four rak'ahs,

like a crow pecking, we get through it and keep on running. No, no, it is the other way round: prepare yourself for prayer – with wudu (ablution), with remembrance of Allah, reflecting on the importance of prayer, setting off for the mosque earlier, standing in the row, remembering Allah a little – and you will see how that is reflected in the heart. And then everything else will be even more blessed, even better; the other things will be achieved, but this is the priority. In Medina, the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, [unclear] an imam in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah, an old man.

But [unclear] the fard of Asr lasted 20 minutes. The fard of Asr lasted 20 minutes. I was discussing that prayer with a colleague and friend of mine, and he said: "Well, that is when people understand that prayer comes first, and then the other things… they enjoy the prayer."

We must seek the sweetness of prayer. You know, people say: "Well, prayer is an obligation for me, it has to be done, it's a debt, I get it over with." No, if you just get it over with, then that is a problem. Then that is a problem. If you do not enjoy the prayer, and if you do not feel good in the prayer, and if you have not found sweetness in the prayer, you have created a problem for yourself and you are in a problem.

Then, when Allah spoke about Isa, alayhis-salam, the Messiah, the boy whom Allah created – Maryam, the purest, most chaste woman, when she gave birth. Maryam, whose name is mentioned in the Qur'an. The only female name is the name of Maryam.

For us she is at the highest rank. No one respects Maryam more than we do. All the Christians of this world do not respect and love Maryam more than we do. We regard her as the symbol of chastity, virtue and piety. She gave birth to Isa, alayhis-salam,

without a man, yes, that is the decree of Allah, jalla wa 'ala. And Isa spoke in the cradle to explain to them that his mother was pure and chaste. "Qala inni 'abdullah" – he said: "I am the servant of Allah." Ataniy…

"Ataniyal-kitaba wa ja'alani nabiyya." Allah has given me the Book and made me a prophet. And He has commanded me to perform the prayer and give zakat. Isa, Isa. The first obligation. The first obligation.
And speaking about other prophets, Allah, jalla wa 'ala, says in Surah Maryam, after mentioning them in detail: "Those are the ones whom We chose and honoured" – the prophets and messengers.

There is no one more distinguished than them. There is no one more distinguished, more respected than them. They are the elite. They are the foremost, who came from the offspring of Adam, and from those whom We carried in the ark with Nuh, from the offspring of Ibrahim and Israel – that is Ya'qub – and many others whom We chose. They are the cream, they are the cream, they are the elite, they are the best. What did they do [unclear]?

He says: when the ayat of the Qur'an, or the ayat of Revelation in general, were recited to them, they would fall down in prostration and weep, they would pray. And then came generations who followed their desires and who lost the prayer. My dear brothers, through your… through your steadfastness in prayer you place yourself in the row of this greatest elite, the world's elite
throughout the history of mankind, at whose head stands Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. You stand in the row with them: with Muhammad, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and the other prophets and messengers.

The greatest bankruptcy, the greatest loss, is to abandon a single prayer, let alone to allow prayers to just pass by like that. But what will make us persevere in performing the prayer constantly, permanently and continuously is understanding the essence of prayer, reflecting, when you say "Subhana Rabbiyal-a'la," [unclear] what it means.

Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. You lower yourself, while the exaltedness of Allah, jalla wa 'ala, [unclear]. Prayer, humility in prayer, the sweetness of prayer is something that always drives you on.

When you feel that, then even if all the armies of this world were forcing you to abandon the prayer, there is no way you would abandon it. And command prayer to your families. You come to the mosque, and this [unclear]. Perhaps you do not need to be told this. But I am telling you this because you should be da'is (callers to Islam).

Not only us hodjas; you should be da'is among your families and relatives. Talk to people about prayer. How many of our people pray? What percentage of our people pray? Two, three, five – if it were that, phew, that would be fantastic.

How many people pray the Jumu'ah? [unclear] of our people pray the Jumu'ah. They pray the Jumu'ah… 300 years. Well, move on, brother. All right, Jumu'ah, look further: the five daily prayers. The other prayers [unclear]. How many hutbas (Friday sermons) have you heard? What does that mean?

People are left with the hutbas [unclear]. A Muslim people, 5% pray, masha Allah, what is that? When the Muslims were proud, they were [unclear]. And then we say: the barakah (blessing) has disappeared. Well, of course. It is sins that [unclear] the barakah and attract misfortune.

In earlier times, when scholars were asked about the status of a man who does not pray, one of them would say: "And what does such a man look like, a Muslim who does not pray? I would like to imagine what such a man looks like." Well, had you lived, esteemed shaykh, in our time, you would have seen people who say "Muslims, masha Allah, love Allah and the Prophet," and who do not [unclear] the prayer.

My dear brothers, prayer is a privilege. Prayer is not a burden – it is an obligation, but it is not a burden. Prayer is a privilege, prayer is an honour, prayer is elevation, prayer is pride, prayer is freedom, prayer is comfort.

Prayer is salvation; prayer is ease and rest for the soul and the body. The Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, used to say: "Bilal, call the iqamah so that we may pray, so that we may find rest."
Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'anil-'azim.
